problem: End-to-end policies degrade out of distribution, modular zero-shot pipelines such as Modular GOAT are capped by closed-set detector recall, and 3D snapshot-memory systems such as 3D-Mem are heavy, view-dependent and single-agent. None of these gives a lightweight, shareable, lifelong memory that supports multi-robot exploration on GOAT-Bench.
motivation: Home robots must find objects given by name, image or language description, and keep memory across a stream of subtasks. The authors argue that a VLM treated as a noisy oracle, whose scores are fused into a persistent 2D uncertainty-aware map, can replace both fragile detectors and dense 3D memories. Such a map also serves as a natural medium for decentralized multi-agent coordination.
key_idea: Fuse VLM relevance scores into a never-reset 2D Gaussian Bayesian Value Map, rank frontiers by a convex blend of a VLM-as-judge softmax and a Bayesian UCB term, and allocate frontiers across agents by decentralized greedy bidding with a separation penalty.
insight: The architecture drives most of the gain: at N=1 it already reaches 41.9% Subtask SR, above Modular GOAT (24.9%), SenseAct-NN (29.5%) and TANGO (32.1%). Extra agents add +10.5 pp (N=2) and +3.2 pp (N=3) with diminishing returns. The four-way detector ablation shows that as recall rises, failures shift from budget exhaustion (42.3% with YOLO-World) to false stops (80.2% with SAM3). The bottleneck is therefore goal verification at the stop decision, not exploration. The evidence is single-run per cell, apart from a two-seed check of the headline configuration.
method: Gaussian Bayesian Value Map: per-cell belief N(mu, sigma^2) on a shared 480x480 BEV grid (0.05 m per cell). The prior is mu0=0.5, sigma0^2=0.5. Observations come from the VLM score through a depth-cone mask, with sigma_obs^2 = 1 - cone_conf. Fusion is a precision-weighted Gaussian product, and the map is never reset across subtasks.

Perception stack (swappable): SAM3 open-vocabulary masks, with GroundedSAM or YOLO-World+MobileSAM as ablations. SpaceOM-3B is the VLM, and CLIP ViT-B/32 (DINOv2 in ablation) matches image goals. A GoalProjector back-projects detections through depth and rejects spatially inconsistent hits.

VLM-as-judge chain: scene caption, room-type prior, an is-worth Yes/No gate (threshold 0.5, from first-token logits), and an A/B/C/D softmax over up to 4 frontier markers drawn on the egocentric view or top-down map.
Convex-blended UCB scoring: UCB(f)=mu+beta*sqrt(sigma^2) with beta=1.7, min-max normalized, blended s=(1-w)p_VLM+w*UCB with w=0.5. Frontiers are re-evaluated every 25 steps.

Decentralized sequential greedy allocator: agents bid in fixed order, with a x0.6 penalty for frontiers within 100 px of earlier agents' picks. A 1.5x commitment hysteresis prevents oscillation. Coordination happens only through the shared BEV (element-wise max) and BVM (Gaussian product).

Planning and STOP gate: FMM planner on the BEV outputs discrete Habitat actions. DistGate rejects STOP if the goal projection is farther than 3 m, but accepts STOP when no projection exists (a noted bug).

setting.backbone: SAM3 + SpaceOM-3B VLM + CLIP ViT-B/32 (all frozen); FMM planner
setting.model_size: SpaceOM-3B VLM plus SAM3 and CLIP
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (360x640, 42° HFOV) plus GPS/compass, per agent
setting.simulator: Habitat-Lab / Habitat-Sim (challenge-2022) with HM3D scenes; Stretch embodiment; plus a real-world Unitree Go1 deployment
setting.privileged: none in simulation (GPS/compass are part of the benchmark); the real robot uses Vicon ground-truth pose

numbers.extra: 2 decentralized agents; strict regime (0.25 m steps, 42° HFOV, no teleport); 500 steps per subtask
image matcher swapped from CLIP to DINOv2

numbers_note: Subtask SR is reported as SR. The paper also reports DTG 2.119 m, per-modality SR (Object/Image/Description) and Episode SR, but no main Episode SR value was printed. N=1 is quoted as both 41.9 and 42.0 in the text.
results: On the full GOAT-Bench val-unseen split, AnyGoal with N=2 reaches 52.4% Subtask SR and 12.7% SPL, beating Modular GOAT (24.9% SR) by +27.5 pp and TANGO (32.1%) by +20.3 pp; N=1 reaches 41.9% and N=3 reaches 55.6%. SPL is lower than Modular GOAT (17.2) and TANGO (16.5), and 3D-Mem's 62.9 SR / 44.7 SPL come from a relaxed regime the authors deem not comparable.
limitations: Twelve goal categories (glass, shower glass, etc.) score 0% SR because transparent, thin or specular surfaces defeat depth back-projection; a DistGate edge case also accepts STOP when no projection exists.

Path efficiency is low (SPL 12.7 vs 17.2 for Modular GOAT) and 80% of failures are false stops. Ablations are single-run, and the simulator shares the map in-process, while the real-world deployment relies on Vicon poses and is only single-agent, with no reported quantitative results.
The comparison with 3D-Mem is not like-for-like: it is evaluated under a different regime, and only the strict-regime table rows are directly comparable.
